To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recent multi-modal models are less visually perceptive than their predecessors.
(1) recent multi-modal models tend to perceive visual data less than previous ones and (2) this is concerning because answers are increasingly inferred from textual information only

(i) the perceptual score is an effective tool to analyze and compare the degree to which different classifiers rely on the different subsets (modalities) of the input features; and (ii) recent, more accurate multi-modal models for VQA and VD tend to perceive the input data less than their counterparts, i.e., they tend to rely more on the text than on the visual data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what data modalities does your model perceive?
the following questions. (1) How do models perceive data modalities? (2) What is the impact of the perceptiveness of the model?
the question: How well do models understand the data they are trained on?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The perceptual score is a metric that assessess the degree to which the model is perceiving different subsets of the data.

the perceptual score is a novel metric that assesses to what degree a model relies on a given subset of input features, i. e., modalities, and that it can be used to analyze and discuss model biases and the perceptiveness of models.
we introduce the Perceptual Score as a new metric to measure how much a model perceives the different data modalities of a multi-modal dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel metric called perceptual score that measures the reliance of multi-modal deep learning models on the different input modalities, and we show that the perceptual score is a good proxy for the model’s reliance on the input modalities.

1) we introduce the perceptuality score to assess the perceptual capability of a model, 2) we show that recent multi-modal models have a reduced perception of the visual input compared to their predecessors, 3) the reduced perception can be attributed to the increased reliance of the model on the text input and the reduced reliance on the image input.
we introduce the perceptuality score, which is a metric that measures to what extent the model relies on the various subsets of the input data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perceptual score can be used to analyze the perceptual abilities of a model.
we need to be careful when using multi-modal datasets and models as they can be biased.
recent state-of-the-art models for multi-modal tasks perceive the input features less than their predecessors, i.e., recent models tend to perceive the textual features more than the visual ones.
